arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Landau argued Section 1425(a) authorizes stripping citizenship if procured contrary to law.
Mr. Parker stated naturalization fundamentally changes the relationship between government and individual.
Justice Alito questioned whether being a Serb in Bosnia guarantees asylum rights.
Justice Ginsburg asked how good moral character interacts with immaterial lies in applications.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Elma Maslenjak faces denaturalization for false statements in her application. The government argues any lie justifies revocation. Maslenjak argues only material lies matter.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The government wants to revoke Maslenjak's citizenship based on any false statement.
Maslenjak wants to keep her citizenship because the lies were immaterial.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues Section 1425(a) allows revocation for any lie, regardless of impact.
Maslenjak argues the law requires proof that the lie materially influenced the decision.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the standard for revoking citizenship. It determines how strictly courts scrutinize naturalization applications. It affects the stability of citizenship for millions of immigrants.
